result.title: Knowledge Interaction in Hypernetwork-based Continual Learning: Conflict and Composition
result.summary: Continual learning aims to adapt pretrained large language models (LLMs) to evolving data while preserving their pretrained capabilities. A central challenge is catastrophic forgetting: adaptation to new data can impair performance on previously learned knowledge. Since continual learning commonly changes model parameters, the model's predictions may draw on knowledge from the base model, the parameter update, and the input context. Understanding how these sources interact is essential: conflicts reveal whether new knowledge can override outdated knowledge, while multi-hop reasoning tests whether new knowledge can be composed with existing knowledge to support generalization. We study these interactions in a hypernetwork-based adaptation framework, where a shared network generates adapters from context, allowing a frozen base model to adapt without task-specific updates. We find that, under knowledge conflict, models preferentially follow the context, and their choices depend more on where knowledge is presented than on its content. We also show that context and adapter knowledge perturb the base model's representations along directions orthogonal to its clean hidden states, enabling us to derive steering vectors that control which source the model follows. In multi-hop reasoning, we find that models fail to reliably compose knowledge across the three sources, with the key breakdown arising from the interaction of the hypernetwork with both the base model and the context. Code and reproduction materials: https://github.com/missswiftie/Knowledge-Interaction-in-CL

AI.brief_summary: 论文在基于超网络的持续学习框架中研究基础模型、适配器更新与输入上下文三种知识来源的交互：在知识冲突下模型偏向跟随上下文且更依赖知识出现位置，多跳推理中三者难以可靠组合，并发现上下文与适配器知识沿正交于干净隐状态的方向扰动表示，由此导出可控制知识来源的引导向量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其表示几何与引导向量「控制模型遵循哪个知识来源」的技术，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据与语言先验的取舍、以及答案是否真正使用 latent 内容；多跳组合失效的分析也或可迁移到视觉证据与 latent 状态的组合与信息坍缩问题。
